filename: So there I was at this party and my friend just wouldnt quit pushing drinks on me I mean it was like a never-ending cycle of peer pressure So I flipped the script and started trying to get him to chill on the drinking The irony was wild It turned int.mp4
transcription: My friend wouldn't stop trying to get me to drink at a party, so I started trying to get him to stop drinking. I don't drink alcohol. In my mid-twenties I made a decision to stop. I felt like I was using it to deal with issues, and I thought it was unhealthy. I had also watched one of my best friends develop a chemical dependency on it and have to go through a long process to stop. Before it became a real problem, I just decided to stop drinking. It was a personal decision, and I didn't and don't really make a big deal about it. If someone offers me a drink in a social setting, I just politely decline and move on. My friends got the message, and I eventually had to explain it to them. They all know my reasons and for the most part they are respectful about it. They will still offer me drinks every once in a while, and I will just say, no thanks, and we will both move on. Except for one friend of a friend. We will call him Greg. This guy will constantly badger me to drink. All come on, just one drink. It won't slime you. You have to drink with us. You have too. Just a little bit. It won't slime you. Last weekend, this guy would just not stop. I even tried avoiding him and it seemed like he was tracking me down. He would hand me open beers that I would have to hand to someone else and pour me shots and just hand the glass to me. I usually just let all of this go, but I was starting to get annoyed. I genuinely do not understand it. Why does it matter to him if I drink? If I pushed my lifestyle choices on him that would be very rude and obnoxious. So, I started doing that. Why are you drinking alcohol? It's bad for your liver. You're having another beer? Water is so much better for you. You probably need some water. I'll get you a cup. You're not 20 anymore. You're going to have a bad hangover. Here, take this water. Drink.
